name: virtual-anchor
description: Virtual scrolling that models position as an anchor rather than a pixel offset: variable item heights, per-item viewport events, and scroll-to-item that lands sub-pixel exactly. Framework-agnostic core, with a React adapter at virtual-anchor/react.
author: gluebi
//: Entries point at source so typecheck, vitest and vite dev need no prior build. pnpm rewrites them from publishConfig on publish.
//development: The `development` condition resolves the instrumented build in dist/dev. It switches the whole export map at once, which is why it is a condition rather than an alias per subpath: a half-applied alias would give a consumer two module instances of a package whose trace sink is module state, which is the same hazard the ESM-only note below exists for. There is no SSR path and no worker path, so a consumer has exactly one environment and therefore exactly one condition set. `types` sits above it so TypeScript never follows a condition into a directory that ships no .d.ts — the two builds have identical types, so one copy serves both.
//peerDependencies: React is needed only for the `virtual-anchor/react` entry, and npm cannot express 'required for this subpath only' — so they are optional, and a consumer of the framework-agnostic entry gets no warnings about a framework it does not use.
//publishConfig: ESM only. No `require` condition, so there is no dual-package hazard: one module instance, which matters because the trace sink is module state. A CJS consumer needs dynamic `import()`.
